column4: toolchain-gated: cleat#1980 item 2 lists a REAL Go and a REAL Python fixture workflow in /api/openapi.json, which means building both -- and the Python build needs componentize-py, which THIS job does not install for ./cmd/... (it installs the Rust wasm32-unknown-unknown target there, not Python). componentize-py is provisioned by the tier-1 Gate's rest shard (scripts/tier-gate.sh refuses to run at all without componentize-py and wasm-tools) and by e2e-cross-language.yml. The gate is legitimate rather than convenient: the test calls t.Fatalf, not t.Skip, when CLEAT_REQUIRE_TOOLCHAINS names python, so a job that PROMISES the toolchain cannot silently skip it. ONE SKIP, TWO SITES: the function has two t.Skip call sites (the toolchain gate and the standard -short guard), which is why skip-baseline.txt records 2, but the toolchain one is checked first and the -short one is unreachable here -- so the count is 1. Measured by name: go test ./cmd/cleat-worker/ -run '^TestTheDocumentListsAGoAndAPythonFixtureWorkflow$' -count=1 -json | grep -c '"Action":"skip"' reports exactly 1 at Elapsed 0, i.e. the toolchain gate rather than -short. AND THIS FRAGMENT IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT THE TEST NEVER RUNS -- the tier-1 rest shard has the toolchain and a tier-1 skip is a FAILURE, so the gate is what proves the property was exercised; this line documents the job where not running is legitimate. Companions: a-real-python-fixture-validates-start-input.tsv (cleat#1981) and a-python-fixture-workflow-deploys-with-a-schema.tsv (cleat#3000) charge the same toolchain.
